gaps.description: No source addressed how AI-generated code impacts codebase maintainability over multi-year horizons. IEEE review notes 'no empirical evidence on how agent-generated code may be maintained in the long term' as a research gap.
All major surveys skew Western/US-based. Limited data on AI coding tool adoption and effectiveness in African, South Asian, or Latin American developer communities.

While 39% of enterprise respondents say compliance reviews are more rigorous for AI code, no source provided detail on specific regulatory frameworks (EU AI Act implications, SOC2 requirements for AI-generated code).

Token costs and compute environmental impact mentioned briefly (NVIDIA Rubin targeting 10x cost reduction) but no comprehensive analysis of AI coding's carbon footprint or total cost of ownership models.
No source addressed how AI coding tools affect developers with disabilities, or accessibility of agentic interfaces for visually/motor-impaired developers.
Most productivity gains are self-reported. LinearB's PR analysis is the exception, but no controlled longitudinal study tracking the same developers over 12+ months was found.

contradictions.description: Productivity gains: Self-reported gains (30-40%) contrast with LinearB's finding that AI PRs merge at 32.7% vs 84.4% for manual, and the 19% slowdown for experienced devs in controlled settings.
contradictions.resolution: The gap between 'code written' and 'code shipped' explains this. AI accelerates generation but review/merge bottleneck attenuates delivery gains.

contradictions.description: Trust vs adoption: 84-95% adoption coexists with only 29% trust and 46% active distrust.
contradictions.resolution: Developers use AI because competitive pressure demands it, not because they trust it. The 'use but verify' pattern dominates.

contradictions.description: Junior vs senior benefits: Juniors report higher productivity gains (40% vs 32%) but seniors are better positioned to leverage AI effectively long-term.
contradictions.resolution: Juniors gain from syntax/knowledge filling; seniors gain from architecture amplification. Different time horizons.

recommendations_for_article: Lead with the trust-adoption paradox (84% use, 29% trust) as the central tension
Use LinearB's PR data (32.7% vs 84.4% merge rate) as the strongest quantitative evidence
Frame the senior developer role shift as opportunity, not threat — architecture > typing
Include the 'delegation gap' (60% assisted, <20% delegated) as the key nuance
Address the review bottleneck as the new constraint, not code generation
Cover the security vulnerability data (45% of AI code) as the sobering counterpoint
Mention multi-agent orchestration (Claude Code Agent Teams, Devin coordinator/worker) as the frontier
Note spec-driven development as the professional maturation beyond vibe coding
